cases.description: When the schemaNode is an ObjectNode containing a field "title" with value "Example Schema", getNode("title") should return the JsonNode representing that value.
If the requested field does not exist in the ObjectNode, getNode should return null (the branch that handles a missing property).
When the schemaNode is an ArrayNode ['first','second'], getNode(0) should return the JsonNode representing the first element.
When the schemaNode is an ArrayNode ['first','second'], getNode(1) should return the JsonNode representing the second element.
When the schemaNode is an ArrayNode of size 2, getNode(2) (out‑of‑bounds) should return null.

group: getNode(Object) – array index supplied as String

cases.description: When the schemaNode is an ArrayNode, a String argument (even if numeric) is not treated as an index; getNode("0") should therefore return null.
Passing null as propertyOrIndex should result in a NullPointerException (the method does not accept null).
When a Boolean is supplied, getNode should ignore the type and return null.

group: getNode(Object) – schemaNode is a value node (not container)

cases.description: If the underlying schemaNode is a primitive/value node (e.g., a text node), getNode should always return null regardless of the argument.
When the schemaNode contains a field with a space in its name ("a b"), supplying the URL‑encoded string "a%20b" should be decoded and the corresponding JsonNode returned.
When the schemaNode is an ArrayNode, supplying a negative integer index should be considered invalid and cause an IllegalArgumentException.
A Long value is not a supported index type for array access; the method should reject it with an IllegalArgumentException.
Floating‑point numbers cannot be used as array indexes; the method should throw IllegalArgumentException when a Double is supplied.
If the supplied String cannot be URL‑decoded (malformed percent‑encoding), the method should propagate an IllegalArgumentException.
A Character is not a recognized property name or index type; the method should throw IllegalArgumentException.
Passing an arbitrary Object as the argument is unsupported and should result in IllegalArgumentException.
If the JsonSchema instance was constructed with a null schemaNode, any call to getNode should raise NullPointerException.
